note: Adapted from Roonwal & Rathore 1976; the original is in English. The original uses the old combination Cornitermes silvestrii Emerson, 1949 (type locality Coxipó, Cuiabá, Mato Grosso, Brazil; Emerson 1952 gave the description only later). For this species the original offers only a table of measurements of 3 soldiers (Santarem, Pará) and a comparison with Emerson's measurements, with no continuous morphological description, so this entry gives soldier measurements only; the alate, worker and nymph are not described in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The soldiers described here are slightly larger than those on which Emerson based the species: body length including the mandibles 5.5—6.0 mm; head length to the base of the mandibles 2.20—2.25 mm; head length to the tip of the frontal tube 2.00—2.10 mm; frontal tube length 0.33—0.38 mm; maximum head width 1.63—1.68 mm; right mandible length 1.00 mm; left mandible length 0.75—1.00 mm; antenna 15-segmented. Compared with Emerson's (1952) original measurements: head length to the base of the mandibles 2.20—2.25 mm versus 2.00—2.07 mm; head length to the tip of the frontal tube 2.00—2.10 mm versus 1.83—1.94 mm; maximum head width 1.63—1.68 mm versus 1.40—1.46 mm.
